answer: Each identity must lock a bond before it can act, so creating a thousand clones costs a thousand deposits. When the network detects a cluster of accounts sharing one pattern of behavior, it slashes their bonds, seizing the collateral and burning it. A sybil farm therefore risks real capital at the very dawn of its scheme and loses it the moment the pattern surfaces, while an honest operator on the ridge of ordinary activity never forfeits a pigment of stake.
